newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end lower led by palladium.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end lower led by palladium.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended lower on Monday led by palladium which managed to claw back some losses after tumbling by their 24 yen per gram daily limit at the opening, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from three yen to 11 yen per gram lower, with benchmark April ending off 10 yen at 1,279 yen.
Benchmark April palladium closed 21 yen weaker at 584 yen.

"Palladium opened sharply lower on expectations that Russia will resume PGM exports soon, but prices were lifted off lows on short-covering amid uncertainty over the timing of Russian shipments and the quantity of metal available," a trader said.
Long-awaited talks between Japan and Russia on PGM export contracts for 1997 have finally started in Tokyo.
"Even if Russia resumes PGM shipments in June, tightness in the spot market caused by the protracted suspension of PGM exports, would not ease immediately," the trader said.
In palladium futures, trade houses sold futures, while private investors were generally covering shorts, traders said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $343.75/344.25 per ounce at 0713 GMT, down slightly from $344.40/90 in New York on Friday.
Producer selling dented spot gold during Asian hours, while in gold futures, private investors were eager to take profits.
"Sentiment in gold remains bearish. A widespread view that PGM prices have reached their ceiling also undermined sentiment in gold," one trader said.
Platinum futures started sharply lower, weighed down by weaker spot platinum prices, but closed off early lows in line with the yen's retreat against the dollar, traders said.
Platinum futures ranged from two yen to 28 yen per gram lower. Benchmark April finished six yen weaker at 1,385 yen.
Benchmark April silver was off 2.8 yen at 178.2 yen.
